authoring.value:
The clarified region is the right bounded lobe, $D=\{(x,z):0\le x\le2,0\le z\le4-x^2\}$. Integrate first with respect to $y$:

$$\int_{x^2}^4 6x\,dy=6x(4-x^2).$$

The $z$ interval has length $4-x^2$, so

$$\iint_D\left[\int_{x^2}^4 6x\,dy\right]dA=\int_0^2 6x(4-x^2)^2\,dx=[-(4-x^2)^3]_0^2=64.$$

All inner limits are ordered. The original boundary description also encloses a left lobe, $-2\le x\le0$, whose integral is $-64$; it did not explicitly select a side of $x=0$. Selecting the right lobe explicitly gives $64$.
